svg.title: Trusting the installer on a fresh machine — The installer refuses cleanly, fixes its own gaps, and stays interactive even when piped
svg.text: Trusting the installer on a fresh machine
Scenario: The installer refuses cleanly, fixes its own gaps, and stays interactive even when piped
Without curl, the installer refuses cleanly
A bare machine sets itself up

g.text: Given a fresh machine without curl, with the installer ready to run
A barren Ubuntu machine with no curl. The installer needs curl to download its toolchain, so
this is the first thing it checks.

text.tspan: command -v curl || echo "curl: command not found"

g.text: When the installer runs on that machine
The developer launches the installer the usual way. It prints its banner and starts its
checks.
Then the installer stops and says curl must be installed first
The installer stops at the very first check, names the missing tool, and tells the developer
to install curl and rerun. It exits with an error, before touching anything.
Given a fresh machine has only sudo and curl, with the installer ready
to run
This machine has sudo and curl but no unzip — the tool the installer will have to add by
itself. The installer files are copied in but not started yet.
When the installer runs on the fresh machine with no one to answer its
questions
The installer starts and prints its title. Nothing on the machine has changed yet.
Then the installer installs the tool it was missing and tries again
task devsecops:init fails because unzip is missing, so the installer adds unzip with sudo
and runs again.
And the installer stops and explains how to link the project to GitLab
The installer stops on purpose: the project has no GitLab link yet, so it prints the exact
next step. If this message ever went missing, a new developer would be stuck.

text.tspan: No 'origin' remote configured. Add a GitLab remote, then re-run.

g.text: Given a developer follows the README and pipes the installer into bash
The empty copy, with the installer ready to run the documented way — piped into bash (the
output of one command fed straight into the next). Set up off-screen: the test user, the
tools, and the GitLab login.
When the installer says what it is about to install, and asks first
Before anything lands on the machine, the installer says what it is about to install and
what it is for, and asks. task and uv are already here, so it only asks about the two it is
missing.
The question is a plain shell prompt, because the tool that would make it pretty is the one
being asked about. Answer no and the installer keeps going with prompts exactly like this
one.
And the installer still asks what to install, even when piped into bash
Even when piped into bash, the installer still reaches its first question: it reads your
keystrokes through /dev/tty, so the documented one-line command still lets you answer.
Then the piped install finishes and opens the framework merge request
Answering through the pipe builds and finishes exactly like typing the command by hand.
